kicker: FOR NYC FIRMS RENOVATING HIGH-END HOMES
title: AI quote generation with interior design sketches.
description: For premium NYC renovation firms. We implement agentic solutions that combine your pricing, room scope and interior design concepts in one branded client proposal.
lead: Your homeowner is waiting. Your estimator has the numbers, your designer has the vision, and someone still has to turn both into a proposal. Then the client changes a finish. Another revision. Another evening getting the quote ready instead of moving the sale forward.
audience: You run a NYC renovation or design-build firm serving high-end apartment, brownstone or townhouse owners.
You are the owner, head of preconstruction, estimator or interior design lead responsible for getting proposals out.
You already have qualified enquiries and past estimates, but assembling the scope, price and design keeps holding up the next quote.

problems.title: The quote depends on everyone finding time
problems.body: The site notes are in one place, the estimate in another and the design selections in a third. Someone has to reconcile all three before the client sees a price.

problems.title: The homeowner sees a number, not what it buys
problems.body: Your estimate and mood board arrive separately. The client struggles to connect the price to the finishes and rooms they imagined, so the next conversation becomes another explanation.

problems.title: A small finish change becomes a whole new evening
problems.body: The client swaps the cabinetry or stone. You update the allowance, the scope and the presentation—and check that the latest version still protects your margin.

deliverables.title: Build the next quote from the scope you already trust
deliverables.body: The agents prepare line items from your scope library, rate card and allowances. Missing costs and uncertain quantities are flagged for your estimator, so the draft follows your commercial rules.

deliverables.title: Show the interior concept beside the price
deliverables.body: Bring room concept sketches, material palettes and selected finishes into the same branded proposal as the quote. Your designer shapes the direction and approves generated concept imagery. Detailed construction drawings follow your normal design process.

deliverables.title: Give the homeowner one proposal to decide on
deliverables.body: A branded PDF with room-by-room scope, the reviewed price, options, allowances, exclusions and next steps. The homeowner can see the proposed result and the decisions needed to move forward.

deliverables.title: Carry approved choices into the project
deliverables.body: Keep the accepted quote, selected finishes and open decisions together for the design and delivery team, so the project does not start by reconstructing the sales conversation.

workflow.title: Capture the renovation brief
workflow.body: Bring together the approved site notes, photographs, plans, client preferences and room list. Ask for missing measurements or choices instead of inventing them.

workflow.title: Build scope, design and price together
workflow.body: Prepare the room scope and concept pages, then match priced items to your approved rates and allowances. Keep optional upgrades separate from the base proposal.

workflow.title: Review the commercial and design details
workflow.body: The estimator checks quantities, supplier inputs and pricing. The designer reviews selections and visual concepts. Both can request a controlled revision.

workflow.title: Present the approved proposal
workflow.body: An authorized person approves release. Keep the final scope and design decisions available for the next sales conversation and project handoff.

example.label: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE
example.title: One Manhattan kitchen. Two design options. One clear quote.
example.body: After a site visit, the client is choosing between painted cabinetry and a natural oak upgrade. Today the designer builds a concept deck while the estimator works in a separate file. The proposed workflow assembles both options in one package, carries the approved price difference into the quote and flags an appliance specification still needed. Your team reviews it before the client receives it.
example.input: Site notes and photographs, approved dimensions, room scope, finish preferences, your rate card and the current supplier allowances.
example.output: A branded proposal with base scope, priced upgrade, interior concept pages, material selections and a short list of open decisions.
example.reviewer: Your estimator approves the commercial details, your designer approves the concept, and your owner or sales lead authorizes release.

systems.body: Keep the project folders, estimating files and design tools your team already uses. We connect the specific inputs needed for the first quote type and return the proposal in your format.

Approved price books and estimate templates
Interior design references and selection libraries
Your CRM and project-management records

problems.title: You discover the missing item when the work should start
problems.body: An accountant opens the package and finds the wrong period, a missing recurring invoice or an unapproved payroll input. The job goes back into the waiting pile.

problems.title: Several people chase the same answer
problems.body: A coordinator checks email, a bookkeeper checks the portal and a manager asks for an update. Nobody has a dependable view of what arrived, what is missing and who last followed up.

problems.title: You are busy all day without clearing the backlog

deliverables.title: Catch the missing item before work starts

workflow.title: Match and check the incoming material
workflow.body: Propose the client, period and document type. Compare against the checklist and agreed recurring patterns; uncertain matches go to review.

workflow.title: Prepare the next useful action
workflow.body: Draft the missing-item request or internal task, with its source, owner and due date. Keep a late client response distinct from an internal processing issue.

workflow.title: Approve and hand off ready work
workflow.body: The coordinator approves follow-ups and resolves matches. The accountant or payroll specialist receives the checked package and remains responsible for professional decisions.

kicker: FOR U.S. REAL ESTATE TRANSACTION COUNSEL
title: AI property document review with source-linked findings.
description: For real estate law firms. We implement agentic solutions that compare property documents, flag discrepancies and put the supporting evidence beside each finding for attorney review.
lead: The client wants an answer. The unit description, plans and exhibits do not line up neatly, and the relevant amendment could be in another PDF. Before your attorney can assess the issue, someone has to find the right pages and repeat the comparison.
audience: You work in a U.S. boutique or midsize real estate law firm advising buyers or investors on property acquisitions.
You are the practice partner, real estate attorney or senior paralegal responsible for diligence and client updates.
Your team repeatedly compares similar document packages in a defined jurisdiction, with a qualified attorney responsible for the review.

problems.title: Every comparison means opening the same files again
problems.body: A unit description or parking reference appears across several documents. Each cross-check means finding the matching passage, exhibit and amendment before you can assess the difference.

problems.title: The summary still sends the attorney back to page one
problems.body: A note says there may be a discrepancy, but the supporting pages are missing. The attorney repeats the search to understand the issue and verify what the preparer found.

problems.title: An unanswered question becomes a late request
problems.body: A missing exhibit or unclear scan surfaces near the client deadline. Your team has to request clarification while explaining why the answer is still pending.

deliverables.title: Stop rebuilding the checklist for similar matters
deliverables.body: Your qualified reviewer defines the jurisdiction, eligible document package, fields to compare and questions that belong in the first version.

deliverables.title: Check a finding without hunting for its source
deliverables.body: A comparison table and findings with source references, pages and relevant excerpts or crops. Clearly distinguish supported matches, potential discrepancies and items not determined.

deliverables.title: Keep unresolved questions in view
deliverables.body: A concise list of conflicting facts, missing documents and questions for the attorney to assess. Prepare follow-up wording only after the responsible reviewer decides what to request.

deliverables.title: Explain the reviewed findings clearly to the client
deliverables.body: Turn the reviewed findings into the concise format your firm uses to explain the matter to its client. The attorney edits and approves the summary before release.

workflow.title: Check that the matter is eligible
workflow.body: Confirm the transaction type and jurisdiction, then verify the approved document set is complete and readable enough for the agreed checks.

workflow.title: Locate the facts and their counterparts
workflow.body: Extract the specified identifiers, descriptions and attachments. Find the relevant passages or plan areas in the other approved sources.

workflow.title: Prepare the evidence and open questions
workflow.body: Assemble the comparison report, preserve conflicting sources and flag anything the supplied documents cannot establish.

workflow.title: Review and explain the result
workflow.body: The attorney evaluates significance, corrects the draft and approves any requests or client summary. The system does not clear the transaction.

example.label: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE
example.title: The parking reference does not line up across the file.
example.body: A buyer’s counsel reviews a condominium package using a locally approved checklist. A parking reference in one document differs from the corresponding exhibit. The workflow places both sources in the draft report and flags an unclear amendment. The attorney checks the evidence, determines whether the difference matters and decides which clarification to request.
example.input: The attorney-selected transaction documents, relevant plans and exhibits, and the jurisdiction-specific comparison checklist.
example.output: A source-linked comparison, the conflicting parking references, the unresolved amendment question and a draft matter summary.
example.reviewer: The responsible real estate attorney interprets the documents, decides the legal significance and approves client-facing work.

faqs.q: What if our field-service software already has renewals?
faqs.a: We start there. Configuration or better use of native features may be enough. A custom agentic solution makes sense when a specific gap remains, such as customer-specific rules, incomplete source data or a handoff between systems.

faqs.q: Can this work with our ERP, forms and email?
faqs.a: We review your exact systems, access and data first. The first implementation uses a defined set of supported connections or approved imports. We do not assume every system exposes the same fields or actions.

faqs.q: Does the agent decide whether equipment is safe or a repair is required?
faqs.a: No. It organizes reported findings and prepares work for review. Qualified service staff retain technical and safety decisions, and your commercial owner approves pricing and customer-facing work.

faqs.q: Are technician reports included in the first renewal project?
faqs.a: They are a separate module. We can scope finding review, repair-quote drafts and later form preparation once the source records, pricing and supported access are confirmed.

faqs.q: How quickly will this improve the process?
faqs.a: We agree the implementation schedule after reviewing your tools and examples. The pilot compares preparation, review and handoff time with your current process. We do not assume a time-saving or renewal-rate result in advance.

cta.title: Which renewal is still waiting for someone to rebuild it?
cta.body: Walk through a recent renewal with Yuval: the previous proposal, the review and the follow-up. We’ll check the tools you already have and identify a practical first workflow to implement.
cta.label: Talk about your renewal workflow

title: AI investor meeting briefs and CRM updates.
description: Agentic solutions for fund investor-relations teams: capture approved interactions, resolve contacts and prepare CRM updates and meeting briefs for review.
lead: The investor meeting happened. The notes are in an inbox, the contact sits under two company names, and the CRM still shows the previous conversation. Before the next meeting, someone has to reconstruct the relationship again.
audience: US private equity and venture capital firms with a dedicated investor-relations or investor-services team.
IR leaders, operations managers and CRM owners responsible for keeping investor interactions and relationship records usable.
Teams whose approved calendar, email and meeting information still needs manual classification, contact matching or review before it reaches the CRM.

problems.title: The meeting does not become a useful record
problems.body: A calendar entry tells you who attended. It may not explain why the conversation mattered, which fund or organisation it concerned, or what belongs in the relationship history.

problems.title: The right person is hard to match
problems.body: A new role, subsidiary or duplicate company record can leave staff unsure where to put the interaction. A confident-looking match is not enough when the history could attach to the wrong investor.

problems.title: Preparation starts with a search across tools
problems.body: Meeting notes, previous conversations and approved research sit in different places. The next brief can miss a recent interaction or repeat an outdated fact unless someone checks the sources.

deliverables.title: An agreed interaction-capture workflow
deliverables.body: Connect one approved mailbox, calendar or export. Apply the IR team’s rules to propose which interactions belong in the CRM, with a clear reason and the original source beside each decision.

deliverables.title: Contact matching with visible uncertainty
deliverables.body: Search existing people, organisations and interactions before proposing a new record. Show possible matches and missing fields; route ambiguous identities and conflicting details to the team.

deliverables.title: Reviewed CRM updates
deliverables.body: Give a named reviewer a queue of proposed activities, tags and profile changes. Approved updates use the permitted write path, retain their source and expose failed or duplicate operations for follow-up.

deliverables.title: A meeting-brief module when the record is ready
deliverables.body: Prepare a concise, editable brief from authorised relationship history and agreed research sources. Cite material facts, flag gaps and separate read-only preparation from any proposed CRM changes.

workflow.title: Capture the approved interaction
workflow.body: Read the agreed source and date range. Record what arrived and distinguish IR activity from unrelated meetings using your reviewed rules.

workflow.title: Resolve the people and organisations
workflow.body: Compare the source with existing CRM records. Surface possible duplicates, missing contacts and uncertain matches before a record is changed.

workflow.title: Review the proposed update
workflow.body: Show the source, classification and proposed fields together. Your IR reviewer approves, corrects or rejects each item in the pilot.

workflow.title: Write once and prepare the next conversation
workflow.body: Apply approved changes through the supported CRM connection, keep a traceable result and use the reviewed history in the next meeting brief.

example.label: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE
example.title: One investor meeting. A reviewed record. A better starting point next time.
example.body: An IR associate selects an approved meeting and its notes. The workflow finds two organisations with similar names and asks the associate to confirm the right one. It prepares the interaction, participants and next-action fields for review. After approval, the CRM records the update with a link to its source. A later meeting brief can use that reviewed interaction and flag anything still missing.
example.input: An approved calendar event, permitted conversation notes, existing CRM records and the IR team’s classification rules.
example.output: A source-linked interaction draft, resolved or flagged contacts, a review decision and a recorded CRM write result; an optional meeting brief uses the reviewed history.
example.reviewer: Your designated IR or operations reviewer confirms relevance, identity and the permitted change.

systems.body: We begin with the CRM and Microsoft or Google tools you already use. Review native capture and reporting features first, then scope any remaining gap in classification, entity matching, review or handoff. Backstop and Outlook are examples to assess, not a claim that a custom build is always needed.
items: Approved Outlook or Google calendar and email sources
Backstop or your existing relationship CRM, subject to supported access
Permitted meeting notes and document stores
Public or licensed research sources agreed for the brief
systems.footnote: Product capabilities, API permissions, data licences and retention rules are checked before implementation. Access to investor data and CRM writes stays within the approved scope.

pilot.title: Start with one source and a representative set of interactions.
pilot.body: Your IR lead and CRM owner choose a bounded sample, including ambiguous contacts and irrelevant meetings. We compare the native workflow with the remaining manual work, agree review rules and test the complete source-to-record path before expanding.
includes: Check native product features and identify the remaining manual gap
Agree source access, classification rules and required CRM fields
Test exact matches, ambiguous identities, exclusions and repeated inputs
Run a human review queue and verify approved write results
Document permissions, failed-write recovery and operational ownership
measures: Time spent preparing each reviewed interaction
Agreement between proposed classification and reviewer decisions
Correct identity matches and unresolved exceptions
Duplicate records avoided during replay tests
Time to prepare a source-checked meeting brief

faqs.q: What if Backstop already connects to Outlook?
faqs.a: That is the first thing to check. Native CRM and Outlook features may already solve the problem. A custom workflow is worth discussing when an agreed gap remains, such as your relevance rules, ambiguous entities, approved historical imports or a handoff that existing configuration does not cover.

faqs.q: Will it write to the CRM automatically?
faqs.a: The pilot uses a named reviewer and explicit approval before writes. Any later automation needs separately agreed categories, permissions and validation. Ambiguous records remain visible for review; they are not silently merged.

faqs.q: Can we start with meeting briefs instead?
faqs.a: Yes. A read-only briefing pilot can be the first module when preparation is the priority. We agree the source set and output, show citations and missing information, and scope CRM write-back separately.

faqs.q: Can this process historical calendars and notes?
faqs.a: An approved historical date range can be a separate, bounded batch. We reconcile inputs and outputs, check duplicates and test recovery before extending the period. A historical import is not assumed to be part of the first ongoing workflow.

faqs.q: Does the agent decide which investors to approach or what to invest in?
faqs.a: The workflow prepares operational records and meeting context for your team. Investment judgments, fundraising strategy and investor communications remain with authorised people. No investment or fundraising result is promised.

faqs.q: What do we need for the first discussion?
faqs.a: An IR process owner, a CRM administrator and a few representative examples of the manual handoff. Describe the source and required output first; share sensitive investor information only through an agreed access process.

cta.title: Where does the last investor conversation disappear?
cta.body: Walk through one approved interaction with Yuval, from the calendar or notes to the CRM and the next meeting brief. We’ll identify a useful first workflow and check whether your current tools already cover it.
cta.label: Discuss your IR workflow
